runners_data.name: Lord Ragnar
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win over this exact 7f AW Standard trip and 1W1P in similar going; Ed Dunlop's yard is ticking over quietly (1/16 in 14 days) but Dougie Costello is a reliable partner and Lord Ragnar's style-fit here is excellent with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead.
runners_data.comment: Lord Ragnar won last time out having been runner-up the run before, a form line that reads well on paper; he's rated well below his official mark and last of this field on our figures, though, leaving that recent placing hard to trust fully.

runners_data.name: King of Montenegro
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse returning after 51 days off for Brian Meehan (0/13 in 14 days), whose recent form shows back-to-back 9th and 5th on 6f Good — stepping up to 7f AW is interesting but the hold-up style will be severely tested if pace is controlled and the field never truly strings out.
runners_data.comment: King Of Montenegro was runner-up last time out and tops our ratings for this race, some way clear of his official mark; the concern is a 51-day absence and a mixed profile that also includes a ninth-place finish.

runners_data.name: Greek Symphony
runners_data.note: Consistent form figures of 2-3 suggest a horse that runs its race, and Oliver Cole's stable is in reasonable nick (2/14); however, this horse's natural front-running tendency means it is forced into a midfield role it does not suit, requiring adaptation that short-priced 2yo form horses rarely deliver off just a second career run.
runners_data.comment: Greek Symphony has been runner-up and third in her only two starts to date, a promising start that leaves her rated six pounds above her official mark; lightly raced and unproven from that small sample, but the placings so far read positively for this test.

runners_data.name: Dei Gratia Regina
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes the ride on this versatile type who has form at 5f, 6f and 8f, suggesting stamina is not a concern stepping to 7f; the style is listed unknown, which adds tactical uncertainty, and 47 days off for a yard that runs at roughly a 10% strike rate (2/19) means fitness is a mild query.
runners_data.comment: Dei Gratia Regina was runner-up last time out, the best of a form line that also includes a fourth and a fifth; the drawback is a 47-day absence and a rating only just above her official mark, leaving little in reserve.

runners_data.name: Crazy Cubana
runners_data.note: Won over 6f AW in her most recent start for Ed Walker (3/39 in 14 days — volume trainer, solid but not hot), and Kieran Shoemark's booking is an upgrade in quality; stepping up to 7f is the key question but her prominent style and tactical intelligence from Shoemark make her the most natural danger to Lord Ragnar.
runners_data.comment: Crazy Cubana is our pick, still lightly raced with just two starts, one a win; she was below that level last time out but returns quickly — 24 days on — with today's distance already in the bank, and the overall profile edges it for us here.

races.paceDynamic: Lord Ragnar is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Crazy Cubana and Greek Symphony as genuine prominent-types in a five-runner field, he should be able to bowl along in front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Lingfield's 7f Polytrack without any serious pressure on his flanks. Crazy Cubana won over 6f on this surface and will likely track Lord Ragnar in second, while Greek Symphony — a natural prominent racer — is redistributed to a midfield position on the map because there are more pace-inclined types than can all slot comfortably near the front; Lord Ragnar and Crazy Cubana are best-placed to actually secure those forward positions. This race shape — an uncontested, moderate-tempo lead with a compact five-runner field — overwhelmingly favours the front-two horses who can control fractions and sustain their effort into the Lingfield straight, rather than closers who need a true honest gallop to reel them in. King of Montenegro and Dei Gratia Regina, as genuine hold-up types, face a significant task if the pace is as measured as this map suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lord Ragnar Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Lord Ragnar breaks well and bowls along uncontested at a comfortable clip, with no rival willing or able to press him.
scenarios.body: Lord Ragnar controls fractions throughout, Crazy Cubana tracks in second but cannot find the extra gear to challenge approaching the furlong pole, and Lord Ragnar's recent AW win at 7f on Standard gives him the profile to sustain his lead home. This shape is the dominant one given the confirmed single front-runner in a small field at a distance and surface he handles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Crazy Cubana Stalks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Crazy Cubana travels powerfully in Lord Ragnar's slipstream and arrives with a decisive late surge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Kieran Shoemark, a high-class jockey, could position Crazy Cubana perfectly off Lord Ragnar's shoulder, timing a run to hit the front close home where Lord Ragnar ties up after setting his own pace. Crazy Cubana's dominant 6f win on AW going suggests tactical sharpness and enough raw ability to steal a march at this slightly longer trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Greek Symphony Runs Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Greek Symphony — unable to secure its natural prominent berth — finds clear daylight late and finishes with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: This relies on Greek Symphony adapting to racing further back than natural, which is a significant ask given the style-fit discount, but Oliver Cole's yard is in decent form (2/14 over 14 days) and the 6f form on Good ground is solid. A steady pace could theoretically compress the field and allow a horse finishing from mid-division to pick off tired rivals in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Exploit Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely dawdling early and the field bunches, creating a sprint finish that King of Montenegro or Dei Gratia Regina can exploit.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape — King of Montenegro has been off 51 days and showed limited form on 6f Good ground, while Dei Gratia Regina steps back to 7f after a 47-day break, and neither profile suits a race where the front-runner is unlikely to be tested. Both need a genuine pace collapse to produce the sprint-finish conditions that would suit hold-up horses in a five-runner field.

watchPoints.text: Lord Ragnar's early break is decisive — if he jumps cleanly and establishes a two-length lead by the 6f marker, the race is likely over as no hold-up rival can bridge that gap at a controlled pace.

Crazy Cubana's draw and early positioning relative to Lord Ragnar will be critical; if Shoemark lets Lord Ragnar build any kind of gap through the first three furlongs without responding, Crazy Cubana risks being left with too much to do over a trip she is unproven at.

Greek Symphony's ability to adapt from its natural forward-going style to a midfield role should be monitored in the stalls and early stages — if it fights for position and uses energy fighting the tactics, its chance diminishes sharply.

King of Montenegro's fitness after 51 days off (no 14-day entries for Meehan) and its record of 9th, 5th on 6f Good suggest the step to 7f AW needs to be treated cautiously; it is only interesting if the pace scenario collapses entirely.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap

runners_data.name: Senor Cortez
runners_data.note: Won over 14f here recently and is the clear pace angle in this race — his ability to dictate unchallenged is the central tactical variable, and his STYLE_FIT flag reflects that he is technically being mapped in a slightly more forward role than his usual pattern, though his recent Lingfield win supports the approach.
runners_data.comment: Senor Cortez won last time out to cap an up-and-down sequence of finishes and returns quickly just eight days later, having encountered today's going before; rated only a shade above his official mark, he sits mid-pack in this field.

runners_data.name: Expressionless
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has won over 12f on Good ground and carries a hood, but this Standard AW surface at 1m5f is a different challenge — best form has come over shorter trips on turf and his last run over 16f here produced only a 10th.
runners_data.comment: Expressionless won five starts back and has both today's distance and going in his locker, rating second in this field and well clear of his official mark; his form has since dipped, though, with modest efforts in his last two starts the one knock against him.

runners_data.name: Percy Jones
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type for the Loughnane yard who has placed over 14f on Good but finds this Lingfield 1m5f AW trip a stretch — no wins on Standard going in five attempts and trainer has had a quiet 14 days with no runners.
runners_data.comment: Percy Jones was third two starts back and has both today's trip and ground taken in before, rating four pounds above his official mark on our figures; he remains without a win in his last five, though, and was only sixth last time out.

runners_data.name: Crackergee
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 12f on Soft for Hughie Morrison and arrives with strong sim-going form (9/12 Standard runs) — a genuine hold-up horse whose best form is on easier ground, and the 39-day gap needs monitoring, though Morrison has sent him here fit.
runners_data.comment: Crackergee won last time out but that was his only finish inside the frame in his last five, and he's having his first run in 39 days; even after that success, he's only rated eighth in this field, with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Educator
runners_data.note: Veteran of 7 who wears a hood and holds a place record over 12f on Good; his best turf form does not obviously translate to Standard AW over this trip, and he has failed to win in eight attempts on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Educator was runner-up last time out and has filled the frame in half of his last six starts, rating four pounds above his official mark; the profile is patchy elsewhere, though, including an unplaced effort, and he remains without a win in that spell.

runners_data.name: Naasma
runners_data.note: Placed four times over 16f at Standard including here at Lingfield, making him one of the more course-and-distance-savvy horses in the race — a natural prominent type who should track Senor Cortez and is well suited by a tactical race over this trip.
runners_data.comment: Naasma is a picture of consistency, never finishing worse than fifth in her last five starts and rated four pounds above her official mark; but with all those runs yielding minor-placed finishes and no win among them, she may find this company just as tough.

runners_data.name: Big Bear Hug
runners_data.note: A natural come-from-behind runner whose best AW form has come over shorter (won over 11f Standard) — the step up to 1m5f is a question, and being pushed further back than the map shows means he needs a truly run race to get involved; 55 days off is notable.
runners_data.comment: Big Bear Hug closed out with a third last time out, rating seven pounds above her official mark; she is having her first run in 55 days, though, and the rest of her recent form — mostly finishes outside the frame — is far less convincing.

runners_data.name: Love Is Golden
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Soft but has zero wins or places in 15 Standard-going runs, which is a damning record for this surface — a genuine hold-up horse who will race at the back, and the going profile here works squarely against him.
runners_data.comment: Love Is Golden won five starts back and, although his placings since have been modest, he rates a big eighteen pounds clear of his official mark — the highest in this field — making him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Mister Daydream
runners_data.note: Won last time over 12f on Standard for the Gary & Josh Moore yard and reappears quickly after just seven days, suggesting connections are happy with him — a true closer who will race off the pace, though the step up to 1m5f from his recent winning trip is untested territory.
runners_data.comment: Mister Daydream won last time out and returns quickly, just seven days later, but he's ranked only ninth of ten in this field; that win lifted him well clear of his official mark, yet he otherwise has plenty to find against this opposition.

runners_data.name: Further Measure
runners_data.note: The standout course-and-distance profile in the field with four wins over 1m5f at Lingfield on Standard going (14/15 sim-going runs here) — a prominent or handy type in this context who absolutely fits the trip and surface, and Mike Murphy's yard has a recent winner in form.
runners_data.comment: Further Measure has been remarkably consistent, three fourth-place finishes plus a win earlier in the run, but he was only seventh last time out and is rated bottom of this field; a lengthy 33-day gap since his last run adds another question mark.

races.paceDynamic: Senor Cortez is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 10-runner field over 1m5f on Lingfield's All-Weather, and with no genuine rival to push him along, he should be able to dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front. Naasma and Further Measure are the only other horses with prominent tendencies and may try to track Senor Cortez, but neither is a natural pace-setter, meaning the early tempo is likely to be steady rather than pressurised. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can honestly place at the rear — Crackergee, Big Bear Hug, Love Is Golden, and Mister Daydream are all true come-from-behind horses redistributed to midfield on the map, but in reality they will likely race further back than their plotted positions suggest, making the true rear of the field congested. A steady-pace scenario over this staying trip benefits horses who can race prominently or in a handy position without expending energy in a battle for position, giving those who track Senor Cortez at a comfortable clip the clearest chance to quicken off the sedate gallop into the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Senor Cortez dictates an unchallenged, controlled gallop and the closers never get into a meaningful rhythm off the slow early tempo.
scenarios.body: Senor Cortez sets fractions he is entirely comfortable with, and horses tracking him — Naasma and Further Measure — get the perfect tow into the straight with energy in reserve; the hold-up brigade, stuck further back than ideal and unable to generate momentum off a slow pace, find little late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Further Measure Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and Further Measure's exceptional course and distance record asserts itself late.
scenarios.body: Further Measure's sim-going record of 14/15 runs at Standard and four wins over this trip at Lingfield is outstanding, and a genuinely run race allows him to sustain his effort over the staying distance; he needs more than a crawl but if Naasma or another prominent type pushes the tempo even slightly, his class at this track becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Crackergee or Mister Daydream manage to find a position closer than their natural style and the race develops a strong enough gallop to suit a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Crackergee arrives on the back of a win and trainer Hughie Morrison has the horse fit enough off 39 days; Mister Daydream similarly won last time and is freshened from a quick 7-day turnaround, and if the staying gallop is strong enough through the middle mile, one of these genuinely talented hold-up types could finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Senor Cortez sets too slow a pace and then ties up in the final furlong, handing the race to a horse who has saved all its energy.
scenarios.body: An extreme dawdle could paradoxically suit a horse like Expressionless, who won over 12f at Good and has the tactical speed to pick up quickly; this scenario requires multiple things to go wrong for the pace-setters simultaneously and is the least likely given Senor Cortez's recent form and controlled style.

watchPoints.text: Further Measure's 14/15 sim-going record at Lingfield Standard over this exact trip is exceptional — if he tracks Senor Cortez rather than racing too freely, he is the most dangerous horse in the race at any market price.

Crackergee and Mister Daydream are both genuine hold-up horses who won last time out — if the pace is too slow they will find nothing late, but if Naasma or Further Measure push the tempo from the front, watch for them to arrive late with more momentum than their map position suggests.

Love Is Golden has zero wins from 15 runs on Standard going — despite being placed on Soft over this trip, the surface record here is a significant red flag that punters should factor into any each-way calculations.

Senor Cortez is ridden by 3lb claimer Jack Callan for John Butler — the weight concession is meaningful at 1m5f, but the key watch is whether Callan can judge the fractions correctly to prevent Naasma or Further Measure from sneaking a lead into the straight.

Big Bear Hug has been off 55 days and is the longest-absent runner in the field — Jim Boyle has a 3/17 T14 record suggesting some activity in the yard, but an absence this long over a trip longer than his best form is worth noting before committing.

runners_data.name: Majestic Wave
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Simon Dow who has finished no better than sixth in five AW starts at similar distances, showing no win or placed in those conditions — the lack of early pace in this race does nothing to help a horse who needs others to do the donkey work in front.
runners_data.comment: Majestic Wave's bare results — seventh, ninth, ninth, unplaced, sixth — undersell him, with our figures rating him well above that record and his official mark, and he's back after 39 days with today's distance and going both proven; only those modest finishes argue against him.

runners_data.name: Split Elevens
runners_data.note: Prolific course specialist for John Butler with two wins and seven places from 13 starts on this surface at 7f, races prominently and should slot just behind The Dark Baron in the ideal tracking position; Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a welcome bonus given the competitive weights.
runners_data.comment: Split Elevens won earlier in this sequence and was runner-up on his prior start, though he could only manage fourth last time. Quick back after 15 days with distance and going proven, he needs to bounce back to that placed form.

runners_data.name: Hour By Hour
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby's charge is a genuine hold-up horse at heart despite the midfield mapping — racing out of its natural rear-running position in a field with too many closers, and its two-from-fifteen record on similar going suggests the surface holds no further fear; the bigger issue is whether it can find room in a compressed pack.
runners_data.comment: Hour By Hour's finishing positions — seventh, unplaced, unplaced, eighth, eighth — read poorly, yet he's fancied by our figures, quick to reappear after just 17 days with today's distance and going both proven; only that run of finishes argues against him.

runners_data.name: Equion
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll runner who has placed three times from nine AW starts in comparable conditions, is another true hold-up type pushed forward on the map; eight-year-old who will need plenty to go right positionally to make his finishing effort count in what is likely to be a muddled midfield.
runners_data.comment: Equion is without a win in his last five, but a runner-up effort remains the clear highlight of that run and he rates our fifth-best. Back after 23 days with distance and going proven, he is competitive without quite pulling clear.

runners_data.name: Pickering Castle
runners_data.note: David Simcock's four-year-old returns from a 155-day absence, which is the most significant flag here — the long layoff makes his fitness a question mark; naturally a hold-up horse despite the midfield position shown, and horses fresh off a long break in competitive AW handicaps often need the run.
runners_data.comment: Pickering Castle has been well held in recent starts — a string of sevenths and eighths — with a third earlier in the run his one bright note. He returns from a lengthy 155-day absence; distance and going are proven, but plenty more is needed on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Rosemary's Rose
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly has placed five times from nine AW starts in similar conditions including two wins, and her placed form on this surface is genuinely solid; however she is a true hold-up mare pressed into midfield by the field's composition, so her chance relies on the early pace being strong enough to set her challenge up from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Rosemary's Rose has been runner-up three times in her last six — including in her latest two starts — without going one better, and she returns after 26 days with today's distance and going both proven, a frustratingly consistent placer who continues to just miss out.

runners_data.name: The Organiser
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes the ride for Mark Pattinson on this seven-year-old who has won once at 7f on good ground; genuine hold-up type displaced into the midfield map, and the tongue tie headgear is noted — 28 days since last run is no concern.
runners_data.comment: The Organiser ran his best recent race when second on his prior start, and rates our fourth-best here. Back after 28 days with distance and going proven, he is a leading danger if he reproduces that placed effort, though he remains without a win of late.

runners_data.name: Bonnita
runners_data.note: Patrick Chamings' four-year-old returns after 68 days off following a well-beaten last on AW, and her best form has come at 6f on Heathwick surfaces rather than 7f AW; a natural rear-runner shown in midfield by necessity, and the absence combined with the trip extension are negatives.
runners_data.comment: Bonnita won earlier in this sequence but has since dropped away, posting a fifth and an unplaced run of late. Distance and going are proven and she returns after 68 days, yet she sits bottom of our figures on that decline.

runners_data.name: Dashing Donkey
runners_data.note: William Stone's five-year-old has shown ability to place on this surface from hold-up positions, finishing fourth twice at 7f AW in recent starts; the redistribution into midfield does not suit a horse who needs races to develop in front of him, and his trainer has not scored in two recent runners.
runners_data.comment: Dashing Donkey has managed nothing better than fourth in his last five — fourth, unplaced, fifth, unplaced, fourth — and though today's distance and going are both proven, that modest sequence leaves him towards the bottom of our figures after 39 days off.

runners_data.name: Kyoto
runners_data.note: Style is unclassified (U) which creates genuine uncertainty about where Mike Murphy's four-year-old will settle — has placed twice from five starts at 6f on similar going and may get a bit closer than his rivals if the race sets up as a dash; the step up to 7f from a 6f base is a slight concern but not fatal on AW.
runners_data.comment: Kyoto has steadily regressed, a promising second at the start of this run giving way to a third, a fourth and now back-to-back fifths. Distance and going are proven, but he sits near the foot of our figures after 33 days off, with little in his favour.

runners_data.name: Dannick
runners_data.note: David Probert rides for Gary & Josh Moore, and the TV visor headgear is noted; only 11 days since last run, and his recent form string shows a horse who has been finishing mid-to-rear of fields even at shorter trips — a hold-up type who has failed to land a blow in 15 runs on similar going without a win.
runners_data.comment: Dannick is yet to open his account in his last five — fifth, eighth, unplaced, seventh, unplaced — but tops our figures, quickly back after just 11 days with today's distance and going covered; the finishing figures are the obvious blot.

runners_data.name: Havana Sky
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners Ed Dunlop's five-year-old who carries a hood and boasts a strong record on this surface with one win and five places from 14 starts in similar conditions; quick turnaround at just seven days since last run, and a genuine hold-up horse who benefits if the tempo stretches the field — the question is whether this sole front-runner's pace is sufficient to do that.
runners_data.comment: Havana Sky remains without a win in his last six — fifth, unplaced, fourth, fourth, eighth, unplaced — but a rapid reappearance after just seven days and proven form over today's distance and going keep him fairly competitive without standing out on our figures.

runners_data.name: Dancing Terror
runners_data.note: Amanda Perrett's four-year-old was absent 76 days but has course-and-distance winning form at 7f on the AW and placed at this track — the layoff is a concern but the raw form level is competitive; a hold-up horse in reality who will need to be produced late and hope the compressed field opens a gap.
runners_data.comment: Dancing Terror was only sixth last time out and has slipped since a second earlier in this run, with a couple of unplaced efforts in between. He returns after 76 days with distance and going proven, but that downward trend leaves him near the foot of our figures.

runners_data.name: The Dark Baron
runners_data.note: Kathy Turner's four-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner with a record of two wins and seven places from 15 similar-going starts — Ben Ffrench Davis claims 5lb and has ridden this horse before; the key tactical question is whether he can dictate at his own tempo against this large field without being pressured, and his style fit tag acknowledges he is racing on the edge of his ideal position in a big-field context.
runners_data.comment: The Dark Baron won earlier in this sequence, with placed efforts on either side of that success, but his last three read fourth, sixth and third — a step back. He returns after 48 days with distance and going proven; our figures rate him mid-division.

races.paceDynamic: The Dark Baron is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner Lingfield AW 7f handicap and, with no genuine rival willing to press him hard from the gates, he should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Split Elevens is the only other horse with a prominent profile, and with The Dark Baron already occupying that lead role, Split Elevens will need to slot in just off the shoulder rather than attempt to match strides. The field behind them is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Hour By Hour, Rosemary's Rose, Pickering Castle, The Organiser, Bonnita, Dashing Donkey and others — who will be compressed into a midfield bunch given the absence of sufficient natural pace to string them out, meaning closers will face a wall of horses when they try to peel wide in the straight. The tactical verdict is clear: a solo front-runner setting a measured gallop on a standard AW surface over 7f at Lingfield strongly favours the horses racing closest to The Dark Baron, as the pace is unlikely to be fast enough to set the race up for true hold-up finishers. Several runners tagged as redistributed — including Hour By Hour, Rosemary's Rose, Pickering Castle and The Organiser — are genuine hold-up horses forced into mapped midfield positions because the field has far more rear-running types than the race shape can accommodate at the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Baron Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If The Dark Baron is allowed to bowl along at his own rhythm and Split Elevens tracks him closely throughout.
scenarios.body: The Dark Baron sets a measured gallop that is neither fast enough to burn himself out nor slow enough to invite a sprint finish, rewarding those who race prominently and make their move from two furlongs out; Split Elevens, with strong course form and a 7f AW record second to none in this field, is perfectly placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If The Dark Baron goes too fast early and fades in the final furlong, allowing the compressed midfield to burst through.
scenarios.body: A quicker-than-expected early gallop — perhaps caused by Split Elevens pushing the tempo — burns off the leaders and the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out; horses who have managed to get closer than their natural hold-up style suggests will be best placed here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crawl Sets Up Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If The Dark Baron dawdles and the pace is so slow that the race becomes a bunched dash in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run affair compresses the entire field into one mass, negating the front-runner's tactical advantage and handing the race to a horse with raw speed off a slow tempo; Kyoto's consistent form at this sort of trip and Havana Sky's AW course experience make them suited to a sprint-style finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Renewal
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses break sharply and contest the early lead, creating a competitive early pace from several positions.
scenarios.body: A contested early tempo — against the expectation — burns off The Dark Baron and favours those sitting just behind the scrimmage who can quicken from third or fourth; Dancing Terror's course-and-distance form and The Organiser's AW grit make them live contenders in this shape.

watchPoints.text: The Dark Baron — if he is allowed a completely uncontested lead from the gate, the 5lb claim on a horse with proven front-running ability could make him very hard to peg back before the winning post.

Pickering Castle — the 155-day absence from David Simcock's yard is the longest layoff of any runner in the field; watch whether the horse shows any signs of rustiness in the market or at the stalls, as a fresh horse in a compressed midfield is a significant each-way risk.

Rosemary's Rose and Hour By Hour — both genuine hold-up types crammed into midfield alongside several similar horses; if the early gallop is too steady, neither will get a run at the leaders and the finishing positions of both will be flattering to deceive the true shape of the race.

Split Elevens — with a 4/19 trainer strike rate over 14 days and a runner who has been out just 15 days, John Butler is in form; watch whether Split Elevens is supported in the market as a strong indicator that the prominent-racer scenario is the one to follow.

Kyoto — the unclassified style tag means this horse's early positioning is genuinely unknown and could influence how the early pace develops; if Kyoto breaks quickly and pushes The Dark Baron wider or faster than expected, the entire race shape could shift toward a contested-pace scenario.

races.name: Follow AtTheRaces On X Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Perfect Location
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on soft/fibresand and placed here on standard, giving her genuine course-distance credentials; hold-up style means she needs at least a fair pace to deliver her run, but she is well-handicapped enough to be involved if she gets a gap.|
runners_data.comment: Perfect Location won last time out, turning around a moderate run of 8th, 7th, 2nd and 6th before that, and tops our figures from stall two — the sole blemish being how patchy that earlier form reads.

runners_data.name: Night Shining
runners_data.note: George Boughey is in strong T14 form (7/34) and Billy Loughnane is a powerful booking, but Night Shining's recent string of four consecutive fourths raises a placed-rather-than-wins concern; hold-up style suits a stronger gallop.|
runners_data.comment: Night Shining has been a model of consistency without threatening to win, finishing fourth in three of her last four starts, and reappears quickly after just 11 days with form over today's trip, though needs to find more to break clear of mid-table.

runners_data.name: Havana Halo
runners_data.note: Best form came over 7f on AW standard going, so the step back to 6f may not entirely suit; a natural closer by trade, she will sit closer to the pace than ideal given how the race maps, reducing the effectiveness of her finishing kick.|
runners_data.comment: Havana Halo's recent finishes — unplaced, seventh, fourth, sixth and fifth — look modest, but she rates well clear of her official mark with us and returns after 20 days with both today's distance and going already proven, capable of outrunning that form figure.

runners_data.name: Court Drive
runners_data.note: Has won over this exact 6f AW trip in similar conditions and her recent form string ends in a 3 (Goodwood) and 1 (soft), showing she can produce; her natural hold-up style means she's shown in midfield here rather than at the rear, and the controlled Autumn Affair tempo is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Court Drive's only win in the last six came two starts back among mostly modest form, but a third-placed effort last time, with today's distance and going both proven, hints she's finding form again — though she remains only an each-way type on these figures.

runners_data.name: Pilgrim's Progress
runners_data.note: Off 208 days which is a significant concern for a two-year-old filly returning to action; natural hold-up horse who will end up racing closer to the pace than she'd like given the race shape, and the long layoff combined with an inexperienced profile makes her hard to trust.|
runners_data.comment: Pilgrim's Progress was runner-up last time out, the pick of recent form that also features a fourth and an unplaced run, but she has not been seen for 208 days. Distance and going are proven; that long absence and bottom rank on our figures leave her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Zooella
runners_data.note: Four consecutive placed efforts on standard AW going — 3-2-3-4 — mark her as highly consistent in this exact conditions profile; prominent-style runner well-suited to sitting just off Autumn Affair, Ralph Beckett has her freshened after 207 days but the placed record rather than winning form is noted.|
runners_data.comment: Zooella has been frequently in the frame without landing a win in her last four — fourth, third, second, third — and rates highly with us despite 207 days off, with today's distance and going already proven; that lengthy absence is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Autumn Affair
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and carries top weight at 136lbs; her 5/5 record on standard AW going including a win over this 6f trip makes her the dominant pace influence, and Harry Eustace's T14 strike rate (2/19) is modest but the horse herself holds all the tactical cards.|
runners_data.comment: Two starts back, Autumn Affair scored for her only win in the last five and has otherwise been placed twice, but was only fourth last time out and returns from a 66-day break out of stall eight, leaving her with solid but unspectacular claims.

runners_data.name: Sydney Rock
runners_data.note: Jack Callan (3lb claim) aboard a consistent performer who has posted three runner-up finishes at 7f on various surfaces; dropping back to 6f on a track where she lacks course form is a question mark, but her prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Autumn Affair.|
runners_data.comment: Sydney Rock ran three placed efforts in a row before an unplaced effort last time, and still rates our second-best. Winless in her last four but a leading danger if that consistent placed form returns; distance and going are both proven.

races.paceDynamic: Autumn Affair is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace pressure anticipated, she should be able to roll along at a controlled, measured gallop from the gates on this standard Lingfield AW 6f. Sydney Rock and Zooella will sit prominently just off her, meaning the pace is real but not contested — a sustainable tempo rather than a war. This shape hands a decisive advantage to horses who can track the leader in the first two positions and quicken from there, with pure hold-up horses needing an unusually strong pace injection that simply isn't coming. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Pilgrim's Progress, Havana Halo, and Court Drive are all genuine closers by nature but are shown in midfield because the race shape will push them closer than they'd ideally like, making their finishing kicks less potent.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Autumn Affair Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Autumn Affair bowls cleanly from the gates and dictates a comfortable, unchallenged pace.
scenarios.body: Autumn Affair rolls to the front unchallenged, posts an even sectional tempo on standard Lingfield AW, and has enough in reserve to repel challenges in the final furlong; her 5/5 record on this surface and going underlines how well she operates here. Prominent runners sitting just behind — Sydney Rock and Zooella — are best positioned to mount any challenge, but neither has beaten a horse in this role on this surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Sydney Rock or Zooella press Autumn Affair hard enough from two furlongs out to wear her down.
scenarios.body: The pace stays honest enough for horses tracking Autumn Affair to take advantage if she ties up in the closing stages, with Sydney Rock's consistent placed record over shorter trips on AW making her a natural beneficiary. Zooella's four-from-four placed record on standard going shows she handles this surface reliably and could edge ahead close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and create a genuine late-run opportunity.
scenarios.body: A genuine closer's scenario requires a tempo faster than Autumn Affair is likely to set given she is uncontested; the redistributed hold-up runners Pilgrim's Progress, Havana Halo, and Court Drive are mapped forward of their natural position and will find it difficult to replicate the finishes they'd produce from further back. Court Drive's sole AW win came over 6f in similar conditions and she is the most likely of the three to find a closing burst if pace accidentally quickens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If there is interference, slow early fractions collapse the field, and the result becomes a sprint finish from a bunch.
scenarios.body: A dawdling gallop compresses the field and turns the race into a flat-out dash from the two-furlong pole, levelling the tactical advantage of prominent runners and gifting an even chance to anything with raw speed. Perfect Location's sole win came over this trip in similar conditions and Billy Loughnane on Night Shining would exploit any positional scramble, though Night Shining's 6-4-4-4 recent string makes her a more likely placed horse than winner.

watchPoints.text: Autumn Affair carries 136lbs as top weight and her uncontested lead is the race's defining tactical factor — watch how cleanly she breaks from the stalls; any stumble or slow start fundamentally alters the shape.

Pilgrim's Progress is 208 days absent and is a natural hold-up horse who will find herself racing out of role closer to the pace than ideal — watch for signs of greenness or early restlessness that could cause interference in a field of eight.

Court Drive and Havana Halo are both genuine closers mapped to midfield; if they attempt to push up early to find their natural rhythm, the race could develop more pace than Autumn Affair expects in the first two furlongs.

Sydney Rock has three placed efforts at 7f but this is her first run at 6f on AW standard — watch her early position to see whether Callan rides her prominently enough to take advantage of her natural style.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Classified Stakes (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Keeper Of Secrets
runners_data.note: Form shows a finishing fade flag on Standard AW and 110 days off the track is a significant query; Charles Bishop takes over for Ian Williams and the horse's genuine hold-up style is squeezed into midfield here, meaning it won't get the patient, deep-drawn run it needs.
runners_data.comment: Keeper Of Secrets has been no better than fourth in five starts and returns after 110 days off, though he does know today's trip; rated near the bottom of this field, he's hard to fancy on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Love You More
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane reunites with this four-year-old who placed last time out at Goodwood, though that form came on Good ground; the horse's natural hold-up style suits a strong pace, which this race may not provide, and the switch to AW Standard is a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up effort four starts back hints at more ability than Love You More showed last time, when only seventh; she remains winless in her last five starts, though she sits second in our ratings for this race, above her official mark.

runners_data.name: Manton Road
runners_data.note: Best form comes at this course and distance on Standard, recording two placed efforts from eight runs here; Kieren Fox takes the ride and the horse steps out of the stall quickly enough to find a useful pitch — a genuine each-way profile if pace unfolds steadily.
runners_data.comment: Manton Road has strung together a second and a third in his last two starts after a spell of modest form, and returns quickly just seven days later; rated level with his official mark, he remains without a win in his last six.

runners_data.name: Monks Mead
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the field with course and distance form on Standard, recording a win and four places in similar conditions; races prominently by nature and faces no rival for the early lead here, giving George Bass full control of the tempo — the key tactical player in this race.
runners_data.comment: Monks Mead has strung together several frame finishes through this sequence and returns quickly, just 12 days on, rating well above his official mark on our figures; the one blot is his latest start, when he found no piece of the frame.

runners_data.name: Raqraaq
runners_data.note: David Probert partners this experienced eight-year-old who has won and placed on Standard AW, but his true hold-up style means he's been pushed into a midfield slot on this map — racing closer than ideal, and his recent form (7-6308) suggests he needs everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Raqraaq is our pick on a third-placed effort three starts back and a quick turnaround — just 14 days since his last run; he's rated well clear of his official mark, with only a modest recent pair of finishes to hold against him.

runners_data.name: Elenaya
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old trained by Mark Loughnane carrying a fading-in-finish flag, with only three career starts and limited AW experience; true hold-up style is squeezed into midfield here rather than dropped out, which further undermines the chance on what is already a thin form profile.
runners_data.comment: Elenaya has found only a fifth as her best form figure from three starts and is rated bottom of this field, someway below her official mark; she does have experience over today's distance, but there's little in this sparse profile to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Querida Zarah
runners_data.note: 235 days off the track is a serious fitness concern, and the form profile (979-) is modest; Tyler Heard takes the ride for Simon Dow, and the horse's natural finishing instincts are negated by the congested hold-up group forcing her into a midfield berth — hard to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Querida Zarah is having her first run in 235 days and has not finished better than seventh in her three starts to date, leaving her hard to fancy off a rating below her official mark; distance experience is the only thing in her favour.

runners_data.name: Nutcracker
runners_data.note: In career-best form after winning over this exact course and distance six days ago, with three placed efforts behind that in the same conditions; Tony Carroll's stable in strong form (T14: 6/48) and Rossa Ryan rides — the horse carries 140lbs but is the standout on recent AW evidence.
runners_data.comment: Nutcracker strung together frame finishes before winning last time out and returns quickly just six days on, off 140lb from stall two; rated top of this field on our figures, with two below-par efforts further back the only blot.

runners_data.name: Celtic John
runners_data.note: Won twice in his career and has AW placed form, but last six runs have produced three finishes outside the top six; Pat Phelan's yard has only had one run in the past 14 days and the horse's hold-up style is further compromised by being displaced forward on this map.
runners_data.comment: Celtic John has a win in his last six starts and encountered this trip before, but his latest run brought no reward and he is having his first outing in 34 days; sits mid-pack on our figures.

runners_data.name: Fitzmaurice
runners_data.note: Jack Doughty rides for Tony Carroll's in-form yard, but Fitzmaurice's last five runs have all been outside the placings over shorter trips — the step to a mile on AW Standard is a new demand; like several others here, genuine hold-up intentions are displaced by the overcrowded rear, not ideal for a horse whose finishing record is already poor.
runners_data.comment: Fitzmaurice's last five starts have yielded finishes between fifth and eighth without a win, and he returns after a 49-day absence; he does have experience over today's trip, though, and sits toward the bottom of this field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Monks Mead is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, should stride into a comfortable, uncontested pace on the Lingfield AW mile — a standard-to-steady tempo that keeps the race together until the home turn. The hold-up brigade is enormous: Nutcracker, Love You More, Manton Road, Keeper Of Secrets, Raqraaq, Elenaya, Querida Zarah, Celtic John, and Fitzmaurice all prefer to race off the pace to varying degrees, meaning the rear is badly congested and many will be forced to race closer than ideal. The field holds more true hold-up types than can realistically find their natural position; of those, Nutcracker and Manton Road — both with proven form at this course and distance on Standard — are most likely to secure a workable pitch, while the redistributed runners (Keeper Of Secrets, Raqraaq, Celtic John, Elenaya, Querida Zarah, Fitzmaurice) will find themselves racing out of role in midfield. A solo front-runner setting a measured pace over a mile on this track creates a classic sit-and-pounce setup, favouring horses with proven finishing speed who can track in the first four and accelerate through the final two furlongs — patient riders who can find daylight from the home turn stand to gain most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Monks Mead Controls, Chasers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead leads at a measured, uncontested gallop and the closers time their runs well from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Monks Mead sets a comfortable tempo, keeping the field bunched heading into the straight, where horses positioned just behind him — particularly those tracking in second or third — get first run and capitalise on the moderate pace; this shape suits horses like Nutcracker and Manton Road who have course form and can challenge at the top of the straight without being blocked.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Monks Mead Steals, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that Monks Mead builds an unassailable lead and the closers leave it too late.
scenarios.body: With a field so heavily loaded with hold-up types, the rear becomes a traffic problem and by the time the closers thread through, Monks Mead's lead is insurmountable; this rewards the one true front-runner in the race, especially if his rider George Bass is allowed to control the fractions entirely unchallenged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead goes too slowly and the closers find a clear passage through a compressed finish.
scenarios.body: A slow tempo compresses the field into a cluster rounding the home turn, and a horse with genuine finishing speed arriving late from midfield — where many of the redistributed hold-up types are forced to race — could thread through a gap; Nutcracker, who won his last start over this course and distance, and Love You More, with a recent placed effort, have the form to benefit if gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Backmarkers Struggle
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo collapses entirely and the true hold-up types left deep never reach the principals.
scenarios.body: The heavily congested hold-up group fails to make meaningful ground as the race lacks the tempo to bring them into it; horses like Querida Zarah and Fitzmaurice, who carry fading-in-finish flags and poor form on the going, are most exposed in this shape, and only those who managed to get a forward position from the gate benefit.

watchPoints.text: Monks Mead is the only horse guaranteed a lead and a comfortable gallop — if George Bass is allowed to dictate unchallenged from stall 4, this front-runner could build a potentially decisive advantage before the home straight and prove very hard to catch.

Nutcracker arrives here just six days after winning over this exact course and distance, in the best form of his career; Rossa Ryan will know the track well and the horse's weight (140lbs) is the only query in what otherwise looks a strong profile for this shape.

The hold-up group (Keeper Of Secrets, Raqraaq, Celtic John, Elenaya, Querida Zarah, Fitzmaurice) all want to race from the rear but are mapped into midfield — watch for significant traffic and interference rounding the home turn as up to six horses try to find room at once.

Love You More finished second at Goodwood 14 days ago but that run came on Good turf; the switch to AW Standard is the key unknown for Billy Loughnane's mount, and if the surface doesn't suit, the recent form could be misleading.

Querida Zarah returns after 235 days off the track with a form string of 979- and no win or place on record — monitor in-running to see whether this filly is fit enough to mount any challenge, as a cold reappearance run would confirm the fitness concern.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Classified Stakes (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Masqool
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer for Tony Carroll with strong standard-going form (11 runs, 3 placed), Dougie Costello takes the ride; the 22-day break is straightforward and the 1m trip is entirely workable, making this one of the more rounded contenders if the finish compresses.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to land a win in six starts this campaign, but a pair of fourths and a third show he has been competitive, and he tops our figures for this race by some margin. He returns 22 days after his latest run with form over today's distance and going, though the main knock is a below-par eighth two starts back.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Sign
runners_data.note: Mark Pattinson's 8yo carries clean standard-going credentials at 7-8f and slots in naturally off the pace; placed on two similar standard trips recently, though racing effectively out of position means its truest form may not surface — the 7lb claimer Slater adds an element of unpredictability.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently competitive without getting his head in front, this gelding's last five runs read second, fourth, fifth, third and sixth. He is back 34 days after that effort, has form over today's distance and going, and a rating of 50 - fifth of nine - keeps him firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Turpin
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave partners this 4yo for Jim Boyle but the flagged fading tendency in finishing is a material concern, and the sim-going record of 0 wins from 3 runs at this trip level does not inspire confidence; the 12-day turnaround is quick and the preference for variety in going (v) is noted.|
runners_data.comment: Turpin has a pair of fifths among his last five starts, showing he retains ability without yet landing a win, and he returns quickly, just 12 days after his latest run, with form over today's distance and going in his favour. A well-beaten ninth last time out is the obvious concern, but he still sits third of nine on our figures among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Zaltalla
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane is a strong booking for Michael Attwater's 5yo, whose AW standard-going record (11 runs, 1 win, 2 placed) shows latent ability; the 165-day layoff is the dominant concern here — a horse competing without a recent run in a race that could demand instant sprint acceleration is vulnerable — and its true closing style is squeezed by the field's character.|
runners_data.comment: A fourth is the highlight of a modest five-run sequence without a win, but this gelding does have form over today's distance and going. The concern is a lengthy 165-day absence since his last outing, though a rating of 51 - fourth of nine - still puts him among the leading dangers on form shown.

runners_data.name: Henfield
runners_data.note: Karen Jewell's 3yo is lightly framed at 126lbs and showed a placed effort over 8f Standard last time; the fading flag is meaningful for a race likely decided in a sprint, and the soft/good ground history suggests AW form is still being established — headgear (p) worn.|
runners_data.comment: A runner-up finish last time out is the clear form highlight for this filly, even though she remains without a win in her last five starts. Quick to back up seven days later, with form over today's distance and going, a rating of 52 - second of nine - makes her a leading contender, despite modest form before that placed effort.

runners_data.name: Miss Gold
runners_data.note: David Flood's lightly-raced 3yo has a thin form profile — 3 runs, no wins, struggling on good and standard — and the 8f trip is familiar but the form string offers little encouragement; carrying 126lbs is an advantage on paper, though the horse's profile as a deep hold-up type in a race of deep hold-up types is structurally awkward.|
runners_data.comment: Three starts have brought a ninth, an unplaced effort and an eighth for this filly, without a win among them, and she sits bottom of our figures in this field. She returns 20 days after her latest run, and though she has form over today's distance and going, a rating of just 23 leaves her with a mountain to climb.

runners_data.name: Conquest Of Power
runners_data.note: Mark Usher's 6yo is the most proven of the redistributed cluster, with 2 wins and 5 places from 13 Standard starts — genuine AW form — though those successes came almost entirely at 6f and this step to 1m against a wall of closers asks a new question; Paddy Bradley rides and the 71-day break merits watching in-running.|
runners_data.comment: A mixed level of form reading fourth, eighth, third, ninth and sixth, without a win in that run, leaves this gelding needing more consistency. A break of 71 days is a concern, though he does have form over today's distance and going and races from stall six off a rating of 50.

runners_data.name: Freedom Bay
runners_data.note: Zoe Hawkins' 4yo arrives on the back of a win over 8f on Good and carries tp headgear; the 30-day rest is routine, and the fact this horse has won over a longer trip on Good suggests stamina is not a concern — most likely to end up positionally forward by accident in this no-pace scenario, which could be decisive.|
runners_data.comment: Freedom Bay won last time out, bouncing back from a moderate spell that had produced finishes of unplaced, seventh, fifth and fourth. She returns 30 days on with form over today's distance and going, but a rating of only 49 - seventh of nine - makes her hard to trust on figures alone.

runners_data.name: Launceston
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan is a high-quality jockey appointment for Joe Ponting's 4yo, though the sim-going record of 0 wins from 4 Standard starts and a form string anchored in longer trips (10-20f) raises a legitimate question about whether 1m on AW is genuinely in this horse's wheelhouse; its hold-up nature in a hold-up field means it will need racing room.|
runners_data.comment: Launceston has faded through his last five, down to a well-beaten seventh last time out from a much earlier second. He returns after 42 days with distance and going proven, but a rating of only 47 — eighth of nine — leaves plenty to prove; still without a win in the run.

races.paceDynamic: This is a field of nine genuine hold-up horses with no confirmed front-runner, meaning the race will almost certainly begin at a crawl as every runner waits for something else to force the pace — a slow-burn mile on Lingfield AW that drifts into a bunched, sprint-like finish from two furlongs out. With Masqool, Rainbow Sign, Turpin, Freedom Bay, and the entire redistributed cluster of Zaltalla, Henfield, Miss Gold, Conquest Of Power, and Launceston all wanting to sit and wait, there is simply no natural pace-maker to set the tempo — the pace dynamic note is explicit that this field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate, and the horses most likely to end up furthest forward by default are Freedom Bay (who showed a win last time out and has a recent tactical profile suggesting positional flexibility) and Masqool (experienced enough to adapt). In a race run this way, late closers with a sharp turn of foot for a short burst are favoured, but the paradox here is that almost everyone is that type, so the horse that best handles a compressed, sprint-style finish on Lingfield's distinctive Polytrack will hold the advantage — that profile belongs firmly to those with proven standard-going form at this venue and the tactical discipline to find clear daylight in a wall-to-wall cavalry charge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dawdle Then Dash
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles through the early stages and the race becomes a 2f sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: The entire nine-runner field converges in the straight having been held up through a falsely-run mile, producing a chaotic, stamina-irrelevant dash to the line; horses with sharp acceleration on Standard Polytrack and a good draw or early reaction are at a premium.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stronger Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If a slightly stronger gallop develops mid-race and the race tests genuine 1m stamina rather than finishing speed.
scenarios.body: One or two horses push forward from halfway to inject some honest pace, stretching the field and rewarding those with true staying power over this mile trip on AW; horses who have placed over 10f in similar conditions are given a chance to grind the sprint-types down.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If a runner from a high draw exploits the inside rail position on Lingfield AW and kicks clear earlier than expected.
scenarios.body: Lingfield's unique configuration can see a horse with positional luck slot into an unchallenged role and use the bend to establish a clear lead entering the straight; the field's collective tendency to wait means a bold-going runner who asserts at the half-mile pole could steal a winning margin.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Shut Out
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched finish becomes too congested and hold-up horses cannot find a clear run through traffic.
scenarios.body: With so many horses wanting to come from off the pace, those held up deepest find themselves blocked and unable to strike; in this shape, winners are those who either tracked closer than usual or found the widest gap soonest.

watchPoints.text: Freedom Bay and Masqool — watch both in the early stages; if either moves forward voluntarily from the first furlong, they effectively become front-runners in a field with no pace, and could steal this from the front with no one willing to follow.

Zaltalla's 165-day layoff is the longest absence in the field — if it moves sluggishly leaving the stalls or fails to travel fluently in the first half, discount its chance of producing a finishing effort in a race decided in a compressed final furlong.

Conquest Of Power has all its best form at 6f on AW Standard; watch for signs of it being outpaced if the final 2f develop into a true sprint, given the step up to 1m is relatively unexplored territory for the horse.

With nine hold-up horses and no genuine pace-setter, the pace collapse is the dominant risk — watch the sectionals from the half-mile pole; if the tempo genuinely crawls to a walking pace before the turn, the widest draw or the horse with the sharpest initial kick from the home bend will be disproportionately advantaged.

Rossa Ryan on Launceston is the standout jockey booking in terms of raw quality — watch whether Ryan attempts to manoeuvre wider or earlier than the horse's natural style suggests, as a tactical override from a senior rider in a structureless race could be significant.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Charles Morin
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose best AW form comes at 16f; visor fitted, 56 days off is a minor concern, but Paddy Bradley knows the horse — needs a strongly-run race to deliver best closing effort|
runners_data.comment: Charles Morin was unplaced last time but consistent beforehand, with a second the highlight and nothing worse than fifth across his other recent runs. Without a win in this spell, he has distance and going proven and rates our fourth-best — a leading contender.

runners_data.name: Douglas Dc
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran hold-up type who has struggled in similar going and distances recently; Billy Loughnane's booking is a positive, but the sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 attempts is a significant red flag|
runners_data.comment: This gelding's last five runs read fifth, seventh, ninth, seventh and fifth without landing a win in that time. Back 22 days after his latest outing and with form over today's distance and going, a rating of 54 - fifth of fourteen - suggests he's better fancied as a place contender than a winner here.

runners_data.name: Hawaiian King
runners_data.note: Primarily a shorter-trip performer (8-10f) who has been stepped up sharply in distance; true hold-up racer whose redistribution to midfield reflects the congested rear of this field — discount significantly given the trip and style mismatch|
runners_data.comment: Six runs without a win, mostly sixths and sevenths, though a fourth six starts back shows he has some ability. Back 25 days after his latest run and with form over today's distance and going, a rating of 50 - seventh of fourteen - keeps him firmly mid-pack rather than a leading player.

runners_data.name: Pablo Prince
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse with zero wins in 11 outings on similar going; dropped to midfield on the map because the rear is simply too crowded — his true instinct is to settle late but the record here offers little confidence|
runners_data.comment: Without a win in six starts this campaign but rarely too far away, with a second six starts back and a pair of fourths since. Quick to return, only 12 days after his latest run, and with form over today's distance and going, a rating of 54 places him firmly in the chasing pack.

runners_data.name: Blue Birdie
runners_data.note: Three-year-old lightly raced filly with a consistent pattern of fading in the finish, flagged accordingly; the headgear note (p) and AW form of 0W0P from 4 similar runs suggest she will struggle to see out this trip strongly|
runners_data.comment: Nothing better than sixth in four runs this campaign, without a win among them, leaves this filly short on solid form. She was last seen 20 days ago and, rated bottom of the field here, looks to have a lot to find on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Lilykoy
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly stepping up from sprint trips (6-7f) to 1m4f — the distance jump is significant and her recent form at shorter distances on AW is limited; reassigned from rear to midfield due to field congestion but won't be in her comfort zone positionally or over the trip|
runners_data.comment: A string of modest finishes - sixth, fifth, unplaced, seventh, unplaced - leaves this filly without a win in her last five starts. She returns quickly, just 12 days on, and has form over today's distance and going, but ranks only twelfth of fourteen on our figures.

runners_data.name: Make It Up
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has placed three times on AW at 10-12f and handles Standard going well; no wins yet but the recent improvement trend and a capable jockey in Marco Ghiani make this a sneaky player if she tracks closer than her designated style suggests|
runners_data.comment: Two thirds in the book but no win in his last five starts, this gelding's form is mixed, having been no better than fifth last time out. A lengthy 41-day absence and a rating of just 43 - eleventh of fourteen - leave him needing plenty to find, despite prior form over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Mister Pretentious
runners_data.note: Exposed three-year-old with a pattern of fading in the finish and struggling to land a blow; the 44-day absence and weak form figures (00-08) on similar surfaces make it very hard to make a case — redistribution from rear to midfield doesn't disguise the limitations|
runners_data.comment: Well held in each of his last four starts, three of them unplaced, without a win in that time. Off the track for 44 days and rated just 29 - thirteenth of fourteen - he has experience over today's distance but faces a mountain to climb on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Sapphire Dream
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with a 2nd on AW at 12f to her name — the most promising stat in this field; finishes weakly at times but 7 days since last run keeps her fresh, and Liam Wright's claim reduces the weight burden meaningfully|
runners_data.comment: A second last time out, backed up by a third two starts back, shows this gelding retains ability despite going without a win in his last five starts. Quick to reappear just seven days later, and with form over today's distance and going, a rating of 49 keeps him firmly in mid-pack contention.

runners_data.name: Smoker Bellamy
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has two AW placings and a recent second over 10f on Standard; remapped to midfield because the rear is overcrowded, though his natural instinct is to come late — if there is any meaningful tempo his closing run becomes relevant|
runners_data.comment: A second four starts back underlines this gelding's ability, even though he remains without a win in his last five starts. Back 27 days after that effort, with useful form over today's going and a rating of 55 - third of fourteen - he looks a leading contender here.

runners_data.name: Graffiti
runners_data.note: Course-and-distance form includes a win at 10f on Good and placed efforts on AW; Kieran Shoemark's booking adds significant jockey quality, and the tongue-tie is an established fitment — his AW record is modest but the 10-12f trips suit and he handles these conditions|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five runs this campaign but has been competitive, placing third three starts back, and tops our figures for this race. Fitness after 42 days off is the obvious question, though this trip and going hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Alex The Great
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer who specialises in very long trips (16-22f) — the drop to 1m4f is shorter than ideal; Tony Carroll's yard is in decent form but Alex's AW history is winless and the redistribution to midfield masks a horse who wants to be nearer the rear|
runners_data.comment: Without a win in its last five starts and rarely fighting out finishes, form has been modest for this gelding. Proven over today's trip and going, but ranked only tenth of fourteen on our figures, leaving more to find than most.

runners_data.name: Belle Of Kt
runners_data.note: The standout form horse — a winner at 12f on Standard going at Lingfield, placed six times in similar conditions, and her record includes a 1W6P line on AW; Taylor Fisher's riding style and the horse's tactical versatility make her the benchmark|
runners_data.comment: This mare won four starts back and was frequently competitive either side of that, with thirds close by, before a below-par seventh last time out (20 days ago). She has form over today's distance and going and rates a leading contender on our figures.

runners_data.name: Brave Guest
runners_data.note: Lengthy 276-day absence (167 days under current jockey) raises serious fitness doubts despite two placed efforts over this trip; her record does include a second at 16f on Good going, but returning from such a break in a competitive classified stakes is a stern ask — the redistribution to midfield reflects congestion, not a tactical upgrade|
runners_data.comment: This gelding has struggled to find the frame in recent starts, finishing ninth, sixth, unplaced, seventh and sixth without a win. He has raced over today's going before, but a rating of 49 - ninth of fourteen - suggests he's up against it.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field at 1m4f on Lingfield's AW, this race is set to drift into a dawdle before a sprint finish unfolds in the home straight. The field is dominated by hold-up types, with Charles Morin, Douglas Dc, Graffiti, and Belle Of Kt among the most established closers, while the pace map has redistributed Smoker Bellamy, Pablo Prince, Hawaiian King, and several others to midfield positions — though these are genuine hold-up horses who cannot all access their natural late ground. The lack of any horse willing or able to set genuine early fractions means the tempo will be controlled and moderate at best, compressing the field and reducing the advantage of a late run. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical flexibility who can track closer to the pace in midfield and produce a sustained finish, rather than true sit-and-wait closers who depend on strong-run races to deliver their best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Midfield Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the race drifts at a steady tempo and horses tracking in midfield produce the best sustained finishes
scenarios.body: With no enforced early gallop, the field bunches and the contest is decided by those positioned just off a slow pace in the final quarter-mile; horses with proven AW form at the trip who can quicken from mid-division hold every advantage

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely slow early before accelerating sharply late, giving traditional hold-up horses a chance to reel in the field
scenarios.body: A sedate gallop compresses the field so tightly that hold-up horses can close ground rapidly in the straight; Charles Morin and Graffiti, both proven at this trip, are positioned to benefit if the sprint finish is truly fierce

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Horse Steals It Up Front
scenarios.trigger: If a horse — most likely Belle Of Kt or Make It Up — unexpectedly pushes to the front and controls a modest fractions-free race
scenarios.body: An uncontested lead at a comfortable tempo would be transformative in a field of pure hold-up horses who may struggle to close if the leader dictates; Belle Of Kt's recent win from the front at Lingfield over 1m4f makes this a genuine threat

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Scenario Collapses, Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the field is disorganised and splits into factions with chaotic early positioning, creating a tactical mess
scenarios.body: A muddled race with no pace shape favours a horse who gets a fortunate passage and holds on from a forward position; Brave Guest, a notable market mover with strong placed form over the trip, could capitalise on positional luck in the chaos

watchPoints.text: Belle Of Kt is the form reference in this field and could control a slow-run race from a prominent-to-leading position — watch whether Taylor Fisher elects to push forward early given the absence of natural pace-setters|

With 14 hold-up horses and no confirmed front-runner, the early stages are likely chaotic; watch for positional scrimmaging from the gate that could cause traffic issues or force horses wide, particularly affecting Charles Morin and Graffiti who need clear runs late|

Sapphire Dream ran just 7 days ago and carries residual fitness risk, but her 2nd on AW over 12f is form few rivals can match — watch whether she handles the 1m4f trip having spent most of her career at shorter distances|

Brave Guest returns from 276 days off and has had only four runs in total — watch market moves in the final hour; if Sheena West's runner is well-supported despite the layoff, it signals confidence from connections that fitness is not an issue|

Make It Up's trainer William Knight has 0 wins from 11 runners in the past 14 days — a notable cold run — but the horse's three AW placings at 10-12f suggest genuine ability; watch whether Marco Ghiani positions her closer than her hold-up tag implies|
